an3.101:1.1: _Jātarūpa_ here refers to natural, unworked gold, for which the technical term is “native gold” (see also [an3.70:38.4]()). I believe _jātarūpa_ stems from the common Vedic sense of _rūpa_ as “form” or “manifestation” of the gods. _Jāta_ is what is “born” or what is part of the “natural” order. Thus _jātarūpa_ is the manifestation of the divine form (of the sun) in nature. Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad 6.4.25 says that when a child is born, the father whispers “speech” in his ear, then feeds him butter and honey with a piece of _jātarūpa_. He brings into his child at birth the wisdom of the Vedas and the divine radiance. Compare _jātaveda_, which is the divine knowledge brought to mortals in nature in the form of “fire”.
an3.101:1.11: Words from _pabhā_ (“radiance”) in Pali are still influenced by the root sense of “shining forth” like the streaming rays of the sun (Rig Veda 1.21.7). The related term _pabhāta_ (“sunup”) is a word for the dawn ([an3.155:4.2]()). Here too, of all the words in Pali for “light”, it represents that which beams through or shines forth, as gold when impurities are removed, or the heavenly bodies in the dark sky.
an3.101:2.1: This is the stage of ethics. | One might think “bad mental conduct” would be the same as the next item, yet here it is abandoned first. Contexts such as [an6.45:8.1]() suggest that it is the kind of mental conduct that leads to ethical or even criminal misdeeds that need to be hidden, rather than simply unwholesome thoughts.
an3.101:2.2: This is the second factor of the noble eightfold path, “right purpose”.
an3.101:2.3: These thoughts are not unwholesome as such, but can still be an attachment. | “Status” is _anavaññatti_, “making them not look down” ([an4.157:2.4](), etc.).
an3.101:2.4: “Thoughts about the teaching” or perhaps “righteous thoughts”, is _dhammavitakka_. This is similar to the situation at [mn19:8.1](), where Gotama was developing right thoughts, but had not yet stabilized immersion.
an3.101:2.5: Typically, “immersion” (_samādhi_) either means the four absorptions or the even deeper states beyond. This is a rare use of _samādhi_ to mean a state of mind that falls short of absorption, but is a step towards it.
